scope: For a stationary memoryless real additive Gaussian channel Y=X+Z with noise independent of input, variance sigma^2>0, and finite nonnegative per-codeword average squared-input constraint P, asymptotic Shannon capacity is C(P)=C_i(P)=(1/2) log2(1+P/sigma^2) bits per real channel use.
boundary: Definitions17.1-17.3, printed pp.174-175, and Definition17.5/Theorem17.5, p.178. Every codeword obeys its average squared-input constraint; the information-capacity optimization separately uses expected cost. Shannon capacity means vanishing error and unbounded block length, not a fixed-epsilon strong converse or one-shot reliable bits. Complex channels have a different prefactor; bits/second needs a use rate; peak-amplitude constraints are separate. No power bound gives infinite capacity. P=0 permits only the zero codeword. The block-noise sentence on p.178 omits sigma^2 in N(0,I_n), inconsistent with the scalar definition/theorem: import the scalar variance-qualified statement, not that sentence. No claim about arbitrary numerical carriers or non-Gaussian noise.
limitations: Per-codeword power and expected information-capacity constraint must be distinguished.
Source block-noise variance normalization inconsistency explicitly retained.
